献给希恩和科里，
他们是我的月亮和星星。

[P4] 1932年，两岁大的尼尔·阿姆斯特朗偶然观赏了一场飞行比赛。
色彩鲜艳的小飞机，“咻”地一声，飞快地掠过阿姆斯特朗父子的头顶。这些飞机沿着三角形的航道飞行，螺旋桨的转动声轰隆隆地划过天际，听起来好像永无休止的雷声。
这一幕很壮观，深深地印刻在阿姆斯特朗幼小的心灵里。4年后，他平生第一次乘飞机，他紧紧地抓住这次难得的机会。

[P5] 那不是一架比翼飞机，而是一架有3个引擎的客机，大家叫它“锡鹅号”。这架飞机在小镇的机场载客，一次可以载12名乘客。
阿姆斯特朗兴致勃勃地跟随着爸爸登上飞机，坐在柳条编织的座椅上，兴奋地系好安全带。引擎发出一阵巨大的噼啪声后启动了。飞机就这样驶出跑道，缓缓升空。
他们离地面越来越远，人群、房屋、汽车和天地万物都变得很小。“锡鹅号”就像一阵风似的在云端穿梭，自由翱翔。
爸爸始终对嘈杂颠簸的飞行与倾斜的视野感到忧心忡忡。
可是，阿姆斯特朗一点儿也不害怕。
相反地，他开心极了。

[P6] 阿姆斯特朗阅读飞行杂志并学着制作5毛钱的飞机模型。
他做了一个神奇的梦。在梦中，他屏住呼吸，飘浮在空中。下面的人群、房屋、汽车和天地万物，都变得十分渺小。

[P7] 阿姆斯特朗一天天长大，对飞行的兴趣也与日俱增。他的房间里有几百架模型飞机和一沓又一沓的《空中旅行》杂志。

为了买杂志和模型，他去教会的墓地割草赚取零用钱。

11岁那年，阿姆斯特朗跑去面包店打工。由于他个子矮小，总会被抱进面团搅拌缸里清扫。

[P8] 他一次又一次地梦见自己飘浮、盘旋在空中。

[P9] 阿姆斯特朗13岁那年，全家搬到俄亥俄州沃帕科内塔城，住进斑驳的白色小楼。这里离他祖父的农场很近。1930年8月5日，他就出生在祖父家的客厅里。

阿姆斯特朗生性害羞，交友谨慎。不过他的生活非常忙碌，除了上学，他加入了童子军，还在学校乐队和私人小乐团里吹低音号。

他在山坡上玩动力飞机，

去市场和五金商店打工，
也在药店整理药架，帮忙摆放药品。

[P10] 在晴朗的夜晚，阿姆斯特朗会爬上邻居维各·金德的车库屋顶。金德先生做了一架望远镜，架在屋顶上，随时欢迎家人一起上去观赏月亮与星星。
阿姆斯特朗总是一看再看，怎么也看不厌。

[P11] 阿姆斯特朗家附近有一座机场，就在老啤酒厂那条路上。他常常去那儿看飞机起降。有时，还会有人付钱请他帮忙清洗飞机。
可是，光是观赏和清洗飞机，对他来说还不够。他问父母，能不能让他去学开飞机。飞行课程一小时要9美金，他得足足工作25个钟头，才能赚到一小时的学费。
他的父母答应了。
不久，他就跟奥布里·纽嘉德老师一起学飞行。他们驾驶的是一架小飞机。

[P12] 阿姆斯特朗学会起飞，也学会降落。
他学会攀升，也学会俯冲和转弯。
他还学会了在空中飞出8字形轨迹的特技。
他体会到，一个有经验的飞行员，还得有一架飞机，
才能发挥他真正的本领。

在阿姆斯特朗16岁生日当天，他如愿以偿地拿到了实习飞行员的驾驶执照，可他当时的年龄根本还不能考汽车驾照呢。
后来，这位实习飞行员成为战斗机飞行员，又成了测试飞行员，驾驶以火箭为动力的飞机，飞上青天。
最后，他终于成为宇航员。

[P13] 宇航员是受过专业训练的飞行员，能够驾驶太空船环绕地球。当阿姆斯特朗成为宇航员时，科学家已经计划把人类送上月球，再让他们平安地返回地球。几千年以来，人们对月亮充满了无限的想象，总想登上月球，一探究竟。

1969年7月16日，宇航员尼尔·阿姆斯特朗、巴兹·艾德林和迈克尔·柯林斯，一起坐进农神5号火箭顶端的阿波罗11号太空舱里。雄伟的农神5号足有一座摩天大楼那么高，还拥有足够的动力，可以把3位太空人送到距地球约36万千米之外的月球上。

[P14] 上午9点32分，火箭的主引擎启动。火焰从农神5号的尾部喷出，接着火箭发射升空。不久，第一组引擎的燃料耗尽，掉入海里。比较小的引擎接着启动，把阿波罗11号太空船送上绕行地球的轨道。在绕行地球两圈后，最后一具火箭引擎便以时速40234千米的速度，将太空船推往月球。

阿姆斯特朗、艾德林和柯林斯在漆黑的太空中飞行了4天。太阳的光线更热无比，阴影下却寒冷冻人。为了不让太空船的其中一面过热或者过冷，太空船会慢慢旋转，就像烤肉架上的热肉一样，太空人觉得这种旋转像是在“烤肉”。

[P15] 当他们抵达月球时，阿姆斯特朗和艾德林便进入专门设计用来与母船分离的登月小艇老鹰号上，准备登陆月球。柯林斯留在母船上驾驶指挥舱，阿姆斯特朗和艾德林降落到月球表面。

两位太空人在电脑的引导下即将着陆的时候，阿姆斯特朗看到巨大的圆石挡住去路，他立刻改用手动控制登月小艇，闪避障碍。在搜寻安全的登陆地点时，一阵刺耳的嘟嘟声突然响起，警告他们燃料不足。当他们安全地把登月小艇降落到月球表面时，老鹰号只剩下运行几秒钟的燃料。

地球人尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·艾德林终于登上了月球！

[P16] 他们穿着太空服，戴着头盔，打开登月小组的舱门时，月球就在他们面前，宏伟壮阔，空无一人。阿姆斯特朗跨下楼梯，一跃跳上了月球的表面，将特设计的摄影机，让地球上的600万人，同步见证了这一瞬间。

“这虽然是我的一小步，却是人类的一大步。” 阿姆斯特朗对着麦克风说出了这句名言。

这次登月，他要替科学家搜集月球的石块，以供日后研究。工作时，他的靴子在尘土上留下了足迹。100万年后，他的脚印可能还会留在那儿。月球上没有风，没有雨，也没有雪，他的脚印永远不会消失。

[P17] 艾德林跟着步下悬梯，踏上月球表面。
地球高高地悬挂在他们上方黑漆漆的天空中。映入眼帘的是一团螺旋状的白色云团，白云底下，依稀可以看见非洲大陆。
阿姆斯特朗在布满尘土的月球表面漫步，缓缓跳向艾德林。太阳闪耀着明亮的白色光芒。
他们竟然在月球上漫步！
阿姆斯特朗跳到艾德林身旁，两人的头盔几乎相撞。艾德林绽放出灿烂的笑容。阿姆斯特朗伸手拍拍同伴的肩膀。
“神奇吧！”阿姆斯特朗说。

[P18] 1969年7月20日，尼尔·阿姆斯特朗登上了月球，成为家喻户晓的大英雄。

可是，深藏在他内心的，仍然是俄亥俄州沃帕科内塔城那个平凡小男孩的记忆。

这个小男孩热爱读书与音乐。

这个小男孩生性害羞，交友谨慎。

这个小男孩梦见自己屏住呼吸，飘浮在空中。

Dedicated to Sean and Cory,
They are my moon and stars.

[P4] In 1932, two-year-old Neil Armstrong accidentally watched an air race.
Colorful little airplanes, with a 'whoosh,' quickly flew over the heads of Armstrong and his father. These planes flew along triangular courses, and the sound of their spinning propellers roared across the sky, sounding like endless thunder.
This scene was magnificent and deeply imprinted in Armstrong's young heart. Four years later, he took his first airplane ride and tightly grasped this rare opportunity.

[P5] That wasn't a biplane, but a passenger plane with three engines, which everyone called the 'Tin Goose'. This plane carried passengers at the small town's airport and could hold 12 people at once.
Armstrong eagerly followed his father onto the plane, sat in a wicker seat, and excitedly fastened his seatbelt. The engine roared to life with a loud crackle. The plane then rolled down the runway and slowly took off.
As they rose higher and higher, people, houses, cars, and everything on Earth became tiny. The 'Tin Goose' soared freely through the clouds like a gust of wind.
Dad remained worried about the noisy, bumpy flight and the tilted view.
But Armstrong wasn't afraid at all.
On the contrary, he was thrilled.

[P6] Armstrong read aviation magazines and learned to make airplane models for five cents.
He had a magical dream. In the dream, he held his breath and floated in the air. The crowds, houses, cars, and all things under the sky below became incredibly small.

[P7] Armstrong grew day by day, and his interest in flying grew stronger. His room had hundreds of model airplanes and stacks upon stacks of the magazine 'Air Travel'.

To buy magazines and models, he mowed the lawn at the church cemetery to earn pocket money.

At the age of 11, Armstrong went to work at a bakery. Because he was short, he was often lifted into the dough mixer to clean it.

[P8] He dreamed again and again of floating and spinning in the air.

[P9] When Armstrong was 13, his family moved to Wapakoneta, Ohio, into a weathered white house. It was close to his grandfather's farm. On August 5, 1930, he was born in his grandfather's living room.

Armstrong was shy and cautious in making friends. But his life was very busy. Besides school, he joined the Boy Scouts and played the tuba in the school band and a private small orchestra.

He played with model airplanes on the hillside,

worked at the market and hardware store,
and also organized shelves and helped arrange medicines at the pharmacy.

[P10] On clear nights, Armstrong would climb onto the garage roof of his neighbor, Vick Gold. Mr. Gold had built a telescope, set up on the roof, always welcoming his family to come up together to watch the moon and stars.
Armstrong would look and look again, never tired of it.

[P11] Armstrong's family lived near an airport, right on the road by the old brewery. He often went there to watch planes take off and land. Sometimes, people even paid him to help wash the planes.
But just watching and washing planes wasn't enough for him. He asked his parents if he could learn to fly. Flight lessons cost 9 dollars an hour, and he would have to work 25 hours straight to earn the fee for one hour.
His parents agreed.
Soon, he began flying lessons with Mr. Aubrey Newgarden. They flew a small plane.

[P12] Armstrong learned to take off, and also to land.
He learned to climb, and also to dive and turn.
He also learned the stunt of flying figure-eight patterns in the air.
He realized that an experienced pilot still needs an airplane to truly show his skills.

On Armstrong's 16th birthday, he finally got his student pilot's license, even though he was still too young to get a driver's license for cars.
Later, this student pilot became a fighter pilot, then a test pilot, flying rocket-powered aircraft into the sky.
Finally, he became an astronaut.

[P13] Astronauts are pilots who have received professional training and are able to pilot spacecraft around the Earth. When Armstrong became an astronaut, scientists had already planned to send humans to the Moon and bring them back safely to Earth. For thousands of years, people have been filled with endless imagination about the Moon, always wanting to land on it and explore its secrets.

On July 16, 1969, astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins climbed into the Apollo 11 spacecraft at the top of the Saturn V rocket. The magnificent Saturn V was as tall as a skyscraper and had enough power to send three astronauts to the Moon, about 360,000 kilometers away from Earth.

[P14] At 9:32 a.m., the rocket's main engine ignited. Flames erupted from the tail of the Saturn V, and the rocket launched into space. Soon, the fuel in the first set of engines was exhausted and fell into the sea. Smaller engines then ignited, sending the Apollo 11 spacecraft into orbit around Earth. After circling Earth twice, the final rocket engine fired at a speed of 40,234 kilometers per hour, propelling the spacecraft toward the Moon.

Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins flew through the dark sky for four days. The sunlight was intensely hot, while the shadows were bitterly cold. To prevent one side of the spacecraft from overheating or freezing, the spacecraft slowly rotated, like meat on a barbecue grill. The astronauts felt this rotation was like being 'grilled'.

[P15] When they reached the Moon, Armstrong and Aldrin entered the lunar module Eagle, specially designed to separate from the mother ship, preparing to land. Collins remained aboard the mother ship, piloting the command module, while Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the Moon's surface.

As the two astronauts were about to land under the computer's guidance, Armstrong spotted huge boulders blocking their path. He immediately switched to manual control of the lunar module to avoid obstacles. While searching for a safe landing site, a sharp, beeping alarm suddenly sounded, warning them of insufficient fuel. When they safely landed the lunar module on the Moon's surface, the Eagle had only enough fuel left for a few more seconds of operation.

Earthlings Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin had finally landed on the Moon!

[P16] They wore spacesuits and helmets. When they opened the door of the lunar module, the Moon lay before them—vast and empty. Armstrong stepped down the ladder, leapt onto the Moon's surface, and activated the specially designed camera, allowing 60 million people on Earth to witness the moment simultaneously.

"That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind," Armstrong said into the microphone, uttering the famous line.

During this moon landing, he was to collect lunar rocks for future scientific study. As he worked, his boots left footprints in the dust. In a million years, his footprints might still be there. On the Moon, there is no wind, no rain, no snow—his footprints will never disappear.

[P17] Aldrin followed, stepping down the ladder and onto the surface of the Moon.
The Earth hung high above them in the dark sky. What met their eyes was a spiral-shaped white cloud mass, and beneath the clouds, Africa could be faintly seen.
Armstrong walked across the dusty lunar surface, slowly hopping toward Aldrin. The Sun shone with bright white light.
They were actually walking on the Moon!
Armstrong jumped to Aldrin's side, their helmets almost colliding. Aldrin broke into a radiant smile. Armstrong reached out and patted his companion's shoulder.
"Amazing, isn't it!" Armstrong said.

[P18] On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong landed on the Moon, becoming a household hero.

Yet deep within him remained the memory of the ordinary little boy from Wapakoneta, Ohio.

This little boy loved reading and music.

This little boy was shy and cautious in making friends.

This little boy dreamed of holding his breath and floating in the air.

[P7] 本页描述了年幼的阿姆斯特朗对飞行的热爱日益增长，他房间里摆满了模型飞机和飞行杂志，并通过在教会墓地割草和在面包店打工来赚取零花钱，以支持自己的爱好。
[P8] 画面描绘了年幼的尼尔·阿姆斯特朗在梦中飘浮于空中，俯瞰家园，展现了他对飞行的向往与想象。
[P9] 本页介绍了尼尔·阿姆斯特朗13岁时全家搬迁至俄亥俄州沃帕科内塔城，并回顾了他1930年8月5日出生在祖父家客厅的背景。同时描述了他生性害羞但生活忙碌，参与童子军、乐队，并通过打工赚取零花钱的童年经历。
[P10] 在晴朗的夜晚，阿姆斯特朗爬上邻居的车库屋顶，通过邻居自制的望远镜观赏月亮和星星，他对此充满好奇与喜爱，总是看不够。
[P11] 阿姆斯特朗对飞行的热爱促使他向父母请求学习驾驶飞机，尽管学费高昂，他仍努力工作攒钱，最终在奥布里·纽嘉德老师的指导下开始学习飞行。
[P12] 本页描述了阿姆斯特朗学习飞行技能的过程，从基础的起飞降落到复杂的空中特技，并记录了他16岁生日当天获得实习飞行员执照，最终成长为宇航员的历程。
[P13] 本页介绍了宇航员的定义及阿姆斯特朗成为宇航员后参与登月计划的背景，并描述了1969年7月16日阿波罗11号发射当天，三位宇航员进入土星5号火箭顶端的太空舱，准备前往月球的场景。
[P14] 本页描述了阿波罗11号火箭发射升空的过程，以及三位宇航员在太空中飞行四天时，因太阳光与阴影温差巨大，飞船需缓慢旋转以保持温度平衡，宇航员将此过程比喻为‘烤肉’。
[P15] 阿姆斯特朗和艾德林驾驶登月舱‘老鹰号’在月球表面着陆，过程中手动规避障碍并应对燃料不足的紧急情况，最终成功登陆月球。
[P16] 阿姆斯特朗成功登陆月球，迈出人类历史性的一步，并在月球表面留下足迹，这些足迹将永远保存。
[P17] 阿姆斯特朗和艾德林成功踏上月球表面，他们看到地球悬挂在漆黑的天空中，并在月球上漫步，阿姆斯特朗对这一壮举感到惊叹。
[P18] 本页回顾了尼尔·阿姆斯特朗登月后成为英雄，但内心仍珍藏着童年时在俄亥俄州沃帕科内塔城作为普通小男孩的记忆，包括他热爱读书音乐、性格害羞以及梦想飞翔的纯真愿望。
[P19] 本页为绘本封底，展示了登月舱在月球表面的插图，并列出了该书获得的奖项、ISBN编号及定价信息。
